column1: # osmo_refdb annotate report levels: one row per reporting unit, for osmotool annotate --method hmm.

# Decided on the calibration split (positive.calib against negative.train, full-length proteins; results/annotate_calib/), never on the test split (results/annotate/). The rule of osmo_refdb.profile_report_levels.tsv (report_rule.py), at annotate's own settings, without the cascade.
# Rule: gene if every member passes the level test at gene level; else group if the paralog group passes it as one unit; else, member by member, gene if it passes, else none.

# Level test: f1_all >= 0.5 on the point estimate AND in >= 0.9 of 1000 bootstrap resamples (level_support), resampling source proteins (not reads) within each family's positives and hard negatives, seed 42; f1_all_p10/p90: the resamples' 10th and 90th percentiles. Clearing on the point estimate only gives none for unstable.

# Minimum evidence (annotate_min_eval_positives = 5): a level needs that many distinct positive calibration proteins (n_eval_positives; a group's summed over its members), else the rule gives none for insufficient_evidence.

# reason: meets_threshold | below_threshold | unstable | insufficient_evidence. out_of_scope and override do not occur: families.yaml sets neither a scope nor a level for annotate. reason_detail: the numbers behind it.

# f1_all = F1 with every non-background protein called as the unit counted as a false positive (own hard negatives, other families' positives, other families' hard negatives); see benchmark_annotate.py.

# tp..f1_all are calibration counts at the reported level (empty for none). f1_all_gene: per member, in members order. f1_all_group: the paralog group as one unit. cascade_gain*: NA, annotate has no cascade.
# The HMM GA and DIAMOND cutoffs were calibrated on these same sequences, so the numbers are in-sample for the cutoffs (optimistic); the test split is the estimate to quote.
